name: Marshall Pointe Apartments
award: 2024 Federal 4% and noncompetitive state housing tax credits
headline: Lincoln Avenue Communities is building Marshall Pointe Apartments, 260 new mostly one- and two-bedroom apartments for households at 30% to 70% AMI on Marshall Street in Arvada, including 13 supportive units with Family Tree. It won a 2024-cycle federal 4% credit plus $700,000 of noncompetitive state credit from CHFA, with $63M of CHFA bonds.
why_it_matters: One of the larger 4% bond deals in the cycle: DOLA bridged the land purchase through Operation Turn Key and a separate $2M DOLA grant passed through Arvada covers sewer and water connection fees, a fee-relief model other cities can copy.

status.label: Under construction since June 2025 groundbreaking; leasing targeted for fall 2026, not yet confirmed
status.detail: The developer held a groundbreaking on 2025-06-03 and said leasing would start in September 2026; a June 2025 trade report put completion in the second half of 2026. No dated public record found confirms completion or move-ins.

next_step: Watch for a certificate of occupancy and the start of leasing, and the Arvada Housing Authority's project-based voucher contract for 8 units.

key_numbers.meaning: 149 one-, 84 two- and 27 three-bedroom units; 13 at 30%, 208 at 60% and 39 at 70% AMI (averaging 60% AMI, computed).

key_numbers.value: $5,687,557 a year in federal 4% credit, plus $700,000 state credit
key_numbers.meaning: Federal credit runs 10 years; amounts are marked subject to change.
JPMorgan Chase made two construction loans of $63M and $33.7M (about $96.7M); CHFA provides the permanent financing.
Family Tree provides services; 8 of the 13 carry Arvada Housing Authority project-based vouchers.

facts.value: CHFA prints 5170 Marshall St, Arvada 80002; news and the city council coverage give 5190 Marshall St
Mixed resident type, new construction; in a QCT; not in a DDA or SADDA; Section 8 column marked No
4.36 acres, about 60 units per acre; four-story residential buildings wrapping a five-story parking structure with 377 spaces; average unit about 764 sq ft; NGBS Bronze
Two courtyards (one for children, one for adults), fitness center, game room and lounge; about 5,190 sq ft of amenity space
13 units set aside for people experiencing homelessness, with economic, medical, mental health and general services from Family Tree

money.note: 2024 cycle; amounts marked subject to change. National Equity Fund is named as a partner (equity role inferred).
Matches the $63M JPMorgan Chase construction loan (bond-backed loan inferred). Whose bond cap is not stated publicly.

background.text: On 2025-01-06 Arvada City Council approved, 6-0 with one member absent, an intergovernmental agreement for a $2,000,000 DOLA Energy and Mineral Impact Assistance grant that the city applied for to pay part of Marshall Pointe's sewer and water connection fees, at no cost to the city.
DOLA provided $5M of bridge funding for the land acquisition through its Operation Turn Key program; the seller, price and date are not stated.
Lincoln Avenue Communities held the groundbreaking on 2025-06-03 and said leasing would begin in September 2026.
CHFA's 13 units at 30% AMI match the 13 Family Tree supportive units (link inferred).
No public document found shows the deal in CHFA's 2024 competitive rounds (Round One applicants, Round Two applicants or awards).

timeline.event: Arvada City Council approves the $2M DOLA grant IGA for connection fees (6-0)
Construction loans from JPMorgan Chase reported (about $96.7M)

Completion targeted for the second half of 2026
